description: Tuan Tran, Abdullah Braik and Maria Koliou published TornadoNET, a workflow that uses street-view imagery and GIS to classify housing recovery following tornadoes. It includes research software and Jupyter notebooks, with stages for preparing imagery, assigning labels, training deep-learning models and analysing recovery through time. These spatial classifications support housing-recovery assessment. The provider states that users can retrain the models when local building architecture differs from the training data. DesignSafe provides public repository access at no stated charge under the three-clause BSD licence. The repository metadata link a GitHub release and a companion Joplin housing-recovery dataset; those files were not downloaded or executed. Dependencies and transferability remain unverified. A separately catalogued application documents training and validation in Joplin and testing in Mayfield, preserving the distinction between the software and its reported case results.
